input.prompt: The camera itself is completely locked off and motionless like a tripod photograph, with absolutely no zoom, no push-in, no drift, no pan and no camera movement of any kind for the entire clip. The framed 'NO SPARKLING WINE, NO LIFE.' pop-art poster on the wall (a hand holding a champagne flute on a red background) stays perfectly rigid, flat and exactly the same size for the entire clip: its illustration, hand, glass, lettering, ALCOHOLIDAY logo, white border and proportions never warp, stretch, resize, shift position or change perspective, as if it truly is a static print and not a generated image. The only motion anywhere in this shot is the green ivy at the right edge of the frame: its leaves sway gently as if touched by a soft evening breeze; every leaf stays firmly attached and never covers the poster. Everything else in the room, including the furniture, the desk and everything on it, the shelves, the books, the bags, the clothes, the bed and especially the framed poster, is completely still and motionless. A golden sunset in the small one-room apartment of a 23-year-old apprentice designer, warm orange evening light through the window. No steam, no smoke, no haze. No people. All motion is small, slow and calm.
